newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Latin American fears of hi-tech arms race subside.
newsitem.headline: Latin American fears of hi-tech arms race subside.

text.p: Argentine Defence Minister Jorge Dominguez said on Tuesday that Latin American fears of a new arms race had been calmed after U.S. Defence Secretary William Perry promised any new high-tech arms sales would be carefully controlled.

Hosting a meeting of Western Hemisphere defence ministers in the Andean resort of Bariloche, Dominguez told reporters that Argentina's lobbying "for transparency and confidence-building measures and avoiding an arms race in the region ... have had a very positive echo."
The three-day meeting of 32 nations from the Americas and Caribbean, to which Cuba was not invited, ends on Wednesday.
Perry, who left late on Tuesday, said Washington was still conducting a policy review of its ban on sales of advanced weapons to Latin America but insisted there was no reason for concern.
"We do not see these countries as threats to each other and they do not see themselves as threats to each other," Perry told reporters.

The ban went into effect when Latin America was beset by dictatorships and border wars. "Now we have 34 democratic nations and border disputes are becoming a thing of the past. Because of that fundamental change in circumstance we believe it is appropriate to re-examine policy," said Perry.
Some Latin Americans are nervous at the prospect of their neighbours acquiring the latest U.S. weaponry, and regional governments have traded jibes over arms purchase plans.
But Argentina's fears, specifically over Chilean hopes to buy advanced fighter jets, seemed to have been addressed.
Dominguez recalled that Argentina bought 36 U.S. A-4 jets two years ago, without regional repercussions, and that Chile would not take delivery of any new warplanes until 1998.

"What both countries are doing is making sure they are prepared to defend themselves, but neither Chile nor Argentina are taking positions that could harm their good relations," the Argentine minister said. Argentina was also reassured by consensus among the hemisphere's defence chiefs to imitate the U.S. commitment to prior warning of all major arms purchases.

Perry played down fears of a regional arms imbalance, saying it "would have been a very criticial factor 20 or 30 years ago when these countries were involved in border disputes with each other and there was suspicion and mistrust."

He promised that if Washington changes its policy, "we would still have as the watchword for that policy restraint. I do not believe it is in the best interests of the nations in the region to get involved in an arms race and to begin to spend excessive amounts of money on a new generation of weapons."
